newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA COME FROM TWO-DOWN TO TOP TABLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA COME FROM TWO-DOWN TO TOP TABLE.

text.p: Barcelona fought back from 3-1 to snatch a thrilling but controversial 5-3 win away win against Real Zaragoza on Sunday as they climbed to the top of the Spanish first division.
Another sparkling performance by Brazilian striker Ronaldo, who scored twice, and a hotly disputed penalty helped them to a victory over the 1995 European Cup Winners' Cup champions.
Zaragoza went in 2-1 up at half-time thanks to well-taken goals from Gustavo Lopez and Gustavo Poyet and then went further ahead when Lopez scored his second.
Barcelona, whose Portuguese star Luis Figo had netted with a superb first-time strike in the first half, pulled back to 3-2 after Ronaldo pounced on to a Figo through-pass.
But the game took a dramatic twist midway through the second half when a linesman alerted the referee to an infringement in the Zaragoza penalty area.
After a lengthy debate the referee sent off Zaragoza's Xavier Aguado, apparently for striking a Barcelona player, and awarded a penalty, from which Gheorghe Popescu equalised.

With Zaragoza down to ten men, Luis Enrique Martinez broke through on the right to put his side ahead with a blistering shot and, shortly afterwards, Ronaldo strolled through the defence to score his fifth goal of the league season.

With 13 points from five games, Barcelona are two ahead of Deportivo Coruna, 2-1 winners over Real Betis on Saturday, and Real Madrid, who clocked up their first away win in the 3-2 victory at Oviedo.
Real Madrid coach Fabio Capello decided to move striker Raul back into midfield for the game at Oviedo.
The move worked. Raul set up Davor Suker, Predrag Mijatovic and Victor Secretario for goals in the first half before being taken off at the break to recover from an injury.
With Raul gone, Oviedo came back to 3-2 and were unlucky not to equalise, having one goal disallowed.

Brazilian striker Romario got back on the score-sheet with two goals in Valencia's 3-0 win at Compostela and Tenerife celebrated their midweek UEFA Cup qualification by thrashing Sporting Gijon 6-0, their second win of the season by six goals.
